Debug boxes. Opacity is set to zero but can be changed to better understand how the bins are being layed out
The same dash pattern twice, the second started a half-period along, so its gaps fall where the first draws.
A zig-zag stroked with sharp joins. The miter limit decides whether each spike keeps its point or is cut square, and 1 cuts every one of them.
A path mark scaled unevenly about its own anchor, and a second at its natural size behind it. Only a path mark takes these: on a symbol upstream ignores them, and so does this engine.
The same numbers on a symbol, which neither engine applies.
One string per row broken into lines on a slash, with a line height wider than the font would choose.
A right-to-left run truncated: the ellipsis goes in front and the tail is what survives, because the end of an RTL string is where its meaning starts.
The same run left-to-right, for the contrast.
An image stretched to a box it does not fit, with smoothing off.
A group whose outline is drawn after its children, and nudged by an explicit stroke offset. The bar runs to the border, so which is on top is visible.
The same group with the outline under its children, which is the default.
Each bar rounds its own corners, and 'c' asks for 40 on a bar the scale never makes that tall, so the clamp is visible.
One radius on all four corners, and a multiply blend so it darkens the bar under it rather than hiding it.
A Catmull-Rom spline at its own default alpha, which is not a cardinal spline at tension 0.
A cardinal spline slackened by an explicit tension, drawn over the same points.
A bundle, which pulls the series most of the way onto the chord across it. Its 'tension' is a blend, not a stiffness.
An open cardinal spline: its first and last points are not on the curve at all.
An area under a Catmull-Rom spline, whose return leg has to take the same curve.
Labels placed by radius and angle around a centre rather than by x and y, and truncated to a width they do not fit.
A group that clips from its encode block rather than from the mark's own property, with a rounded background. The rule reaches well past the group's width.
The features themselves.
The box geoBounds reported, drawn over them.
A circle whose radius is a fixed number of projected units, which only geoScale can give.
Revenue by product line
Value labels
Fitted into a rectangle 190 by 110 at (10,10). The projection has no scale or translate of its own; both are computed from where the geometry landed.
The same geometry fitted to a size, which is that rectangle anchored at the origin — so this one is drawn in a group that moves it.
A conic equal-area projection standing on parallels 10 and 60, fitted to the same box as the one beside it.
The same projection on parallels 40 and 45, fitted to the same size. The parallels rebuild the formula rather than tuning it, so the two shapes differ.
An orthographic globe clipped at 60 degrees from its centre, so the far side is cut away rather than folded back.
Three cities as Point geometry, drawn at the radius the projection asked for rather than at d3's 4.5.
